## How to use this booklet

This booklet is a map of the whole world of movies. It is not a book of contents: every entry tells you, in one or two lines, what the thing is and why it matters, so you learn something real just by walking through it. Every entry has an ID (such as MOV-01.4) that is also its address on the website.

- **Parts** are the big branches (industries, genres, history, awards...).
- **Sections (MOV-01, MOV-02...)** are the main topics; each opens with a *Before you start* box.
- **Sub-sections and entries** carry a ☐ box: tick it when you have watched or explored it.
- **Film Registers** list landmark films decade by decade, with director, cast, box office and awards.
- **Tags** (#india, #horror, #1950s) and **See also** links connect related pages.
- Start with **Part 0**, twelve two-minute questions that tell the story of cinema.
howto_intro: This booklet is a map of the whole world of movies, from the first flickering films of 1895 to the streaming and AI era. It is not a book's contents page: every entry tells you, in one or two lines, what the thing is and why it matters. A newcomer can learn the shape of cinema just by turning the pages; a movie nerd can check that nothing is missing.
Every entry has an ID (such as MOV-01.4 for Malayalam cinema). The same ID is the entry's address on curioussparoows.com, where each one is growing into its own page.
howto_boxes: **Parts:** the big branches: the intro questions, industries of the world, genres, movements, history, awards, people, craft, ideas, reviews, community, navigation and sources.
**Sections (MOV-01 to MOV-25):** the main topics, each opening with a *Before you start* box.
**Sub-sections and entries (☐):** one or two lines each; tick the box when you have watched or explored it.
**Film Registers:** tables of landmark films, decade by decade, for each industry. They are a sourced selection; the full year-wise lists grow on the website.
**Step 1.** Read Part 0, twelve two-minute questions that tell the story of cinema.
**Step 2.** Find your own country and language in Part 1, then travel to another continent.
**Step 3.** Pick a genre you love in Part 2 and follow its example films.
**Step 4.** Use the tags (#india, #horror, #1950s) and See also links to jump between pages.
**Step 5.** Tick ☐ as you go, and use the tracker at the end.

Knowledge belongs to the people who created it. Every fact here stands on a source listed in Part 12, and every "latest" fact says when it was checked. Where something could not be verified, we say so instead of guessing. Found a mistake? Tell us, and we will fix it and thank you.
